latency_ms.input: random noise 640x640x3 — measures compute cost, not detection accuracy

checks.description: real ONNX model loads and reports non-degraded
checks.oracle_source: onnxruntime InferenceSession on the committed .onnx artifact

checks.description: ONNX inference runs on real frames and reports latency percentiles
checks.detail: 30 frames of 640x640x3, 5 warmup discarded. P50=43.781ms P95=81.637ms P99=174.772ms max=174.772ms. Percentiles are nearest-rank over per-frame wall time, not a mean.

checks.description: confidence threshold is a real parameter on the production detector
checks.detail: threshold sweep on the real ONNX detector over 10 frames: [{'threshold': 0.0, 'detections_over_10_frames': 13214}, {'threshold': 0.5, 'detections_over_10_frames': 0}, {'threshold': 0.95, 'detections_over_10_frames': 0}]. Detections monotonically non-increasing in threshold=True; conf_threshold configurable in __init__=True. On random-noise frames the absolute counts are low, so this confirms the trigger is wired and monotone, NOT that detection accuracy is good; that would need labelled frames.
checks.oracle_source: real PCBDefectDetector threshold sweep, no stub subclass

checks.description: corrupt model degrades instead of returning confident output
checks.detail: corrupt model -> use_onnx=False degraded=True. A detector that reports healthy on an unreadable model would let a broken deploy pass as a working one.

checks.description: quality-rejected frame reports no-verdict, not a clean pass
checks.detail: a 1x1 frame is rejected by check_frame (laplacian variance 0.0) yet infer() returns detections=[]. infer() documents None as 'no verdict' and [] as 'inspected, no defects found', so a rejected frame is currently reported to the caller as a PASS. For a defect inspection system that is a false negative: a camera fault or blank frame reads as a board with no defects. Source: src/vision/detector.py:313 returns [] on the quality-reject branch.
checks.oracle_source: real detector on a frame that check_frame rejects

checks.description: invalid frames are rejected rather than silently mis-detected
checks.detail: 3/4 malformed frames raised instead of returning a detection: {'empty_array': 'error', 'wrong_dtype': 'error', 'grayscale_2d': 'error', 'single_pixel': 'returned normally'}. Any frame that returns normally is reported here rather than counted as handled. See A5b for the case that returns normally without raising.
checks.oracle_source: real detector on empty / float32 / 2-D / 1x1 frames

checks.description: per-camera inference cost stays flat as camera count rises
checks.detail: sequential load: {1: {'total_ms': 44.12, 'ms_per_camera': 44.12}, 4: {'total_ms': 165.06, 'ms_per_camera': 41.27}, 8: {'total_ms': 327.56, 'ms_per_camera': 40.95}}. Per-camera cost 44.12ms -> 40.95ms across 1->8 cameras (within 1.5x: True); implied throughput {1: 22.67, 4: 24.23, 8: 24.42} fps. Flat cost means one board does not slow the others. This is a SEQUENTIAL microbenchmark, not a real concurrent line test, so it does not establish behaviour under thread or process contention.
